newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end up on record high A index.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end up on record high A index.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index ended Monday with substantial gains on buying encouraged by the A share market which closed at an historic high, brokers said.

Investors pumped money into A shares, on the expection that there would be no further official measures in the short term after Beijing's announcement on Friday of a hike in the stock trading stamp tax to 0.5 percent from 0.3 percent, they said.

The A index soared 20.88 points or 3.98 percent to end at 546.02, with turnover swelling to 20.8 billion yuan from 17.4 billion yuan last Friday. The B share index put on 3.88 points or 2.16 percent to 183.50 on turnover of HK$184.3 million against Friday's HK$167.6 million.

"People believe Beijing is unlikely to announce market crackdown measures in the short term to avoid a stock market crash around the Hong Kong handover on July 1," an analyst at China Southern Securities said.

"The A share market rose because the stamp tax hike has been the government's only measure recently to cool the market," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said. "People really do not care about it given the bullishness of the market."
The B shares are likely to extend gains into Tuesday if the A share market continues to surge, analysts said. But they cautioned about the possibility of heavy profit-taking.
On the A share market, hot money was diverted into cheap and medium-priced shares which have performed less strongly than the blue chips, brokers said.
Refrigerator maker Changsha Zhongyi, which has a venture with Swedish firm Electrolux, was at 6.56 yuan, gaining 0.60 yuan at its 10 percent limit-up.
On the B share market, Jiangling Motors Corp was the session's best performer with a rise of HK$0.39 or 9.95 percent to HK$4.31 on volume.
